relations.description: Bangla Academy utilizes the traditional 7-karaka/case Sanskrit model (Karta, Karma, Karana, Sampradana, Apadana, Adhikarana, Sambandha). Modern descriptive linguistics (Thompson 2012, Chatterji 1926) reduces morphological case inflection to 4 structural cases (Nominative -Ø, Accusative/Dative -ke, Genitive -r/-er, Locative -e/-te/-y), classifying Karana ('dara') and Apadana ('theke') as analytic postpositional phrases.
relations.blf_canonical_resolution: BLF models 4 core morphological inflection cases on nominal heads and treats oblique relations via postpositional phrase sub-categorization.

relations.description: Azad (1984) formalizes compound verbs as transformational non-finite embedding, whereas Thompson (2012) describes them as aspectual vector verb complex predicates. Both models agree that the pole verb in -e carries primary lexical semantics while the vector verb bears inflection and aspectual modification.
relations.blf_canonical_resolution: BLF represents compound verbs as complex predicates (compound:svc in UD) with designated pole and vector slots in construction patterns.

relations.description: Bangla Academy describes 'ni' as a past-negative particle attached to simple present verbs. Thompson formalizes 'ni' as an aspectual clitic triggering past perfective interpretation without past verbal morphology.
relations.blf_canonical_resolution: BLF enforces rule RUL-MSYN-NEG-PERFECTIVE combining present finite verbs with particle 'ni'.
